name: Mirske

anatomy.part: top spreader, the crown of the kite
bow-knot where the spars cross, on the kite's centre line
bottom tip of the kite, where the tail is tied on

myth: When Aun first flew the Mirske, he tied a knot in its tail for every winter he had come through alive. By his third spring the tail was heavy with them, and he was proud, and he laughed at the Gale. Tavo heard the laughing. He came down off the Windward Reach like a dropped net and tore the kite from its string. Aun watched it go up with every knot still in its tail. Hesk, at the pole, counted them as they passed her, and she counts them still. Ennu says the Mirske flies over the Reach on windy nights, heavy and slow, and that the children of the islands learn their numbers from it. When a grandmother dies, her family ties one more knot on a small kite and lets it go, so the count keeps going. If you see the Mirske, do not count its knots out loud. Hesk will hear you and ask you to hold the string.
verse:
Kite on the cold wind,
one knot for each winter lived,
Hesk keeps the long count.
